gp.heading: Gross Margin
gp.text:
Gross margin as a percentage of sales was 33.5% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 32.1% for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher sales and the benefit of cost savings from productivity and restructuring actions. Further, 2025 included approximately $3.0 million of incremental planned maintenance costs within the SEM segment.

Gross margin as a percentage of sales was 32.9% for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to 32.0% for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher sales and the benefit of cost savings from productivity and restructuring actions. Further, 2025 included approximately $3.0 million of incremental planned maintenance costs within the SEM segment.

oi.text: Operating income is the primary segment performance measure that is reported to our chief operating decision maker (CODM), which is the Company's chief executive officer. Our CODM utilizes this measure as an input to determine appropriate resource allocations to our segments in the annual planning process and to periodically assess segment performance, primarily by evaluating actual results in comparison to the annual operating plan and forecast. Operating income at the segment level does not include corporate general and administrative expenses that are not allocated to segments, restructuring charges, share-based compensation costs, environmental remediation costs and associated recoveries, asset impairments, acquisition-related charges, mark-to-market adjustments on pension and other post-retirement obligations, and certain other items that are not included in the measure of segment profit or loss that is reported to and reviewed by our CODM. These costs are included in Corporate .

nonop.heading: Interest expense, net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net decreased $2.4 million and $7.3 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively, primarily driven by the benefit of reduced interest rates resulting from refinancing activity during 2025, in addition to prepayments on Avient's senior secured term loan totaling $150.0 million during 2025.

tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text:
During the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company’s effective tax rate was 26.3% compared to 24.5% in the three months ended June 30, 2025, while the six month period ended June 30, 2026 was 24.7% compared to 24.2% for the six month period ended June 30, 2025. The higher effective tax rate in 2026 is primarily driven by an increase in withholding taxes and higher unfavorable U.S. permanent items.

Refer to Note 6, Income Taxes , for further details.

ocf.text: Operating Activities — Net cash provided by operating activities decreased $2.4 million during the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025, primarily driven by higher earnings offset by an investment in working capital and higher restructuring payments.

wc.text: Operating Activities — Net cash provided by operating activities decreased $2.4 million during the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the six months ended June 30, 2025, primarily driven by higher earnings offset by an investment in working capital and higher restructuring payments.

capex.text: Investing Activities — Net cash used in investing activities during the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 of $41.3 million and $39.5 million, respectively, reflects the impact of capital expenditures.

Our CODM utilizes this measure as an input to determine appropriate resource allocations to our segments in the annual planning process and to periodically assess segment performance, primarily by evaluating actual results in comparison to the annual operating plan and forecast. Operating income at the segment level does not include corporate general and administrative expenses that are not allocated to segments, restructuring charges, share-based compensation costs, environmental remediation costs and associated recoveries, asset impairments, acquisition-related charges, mark-to-market adjustments on pension and other post-retirement obligations, and certain other items that are not included in the measure of segment profit or loss that is reported to and reviewed by our CODM. These costs are included in Corporate .

nonop.heading: Interest expense, net
nonop.text: Interest expense, net decreased $1.5 million and $8.8 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, primarily driven by the benefit of reduced interest rates resulting from refinancing activity during 2025, in addition to prepayments on Avient's senior secured term loan totaling $100.0 million in 2026 and $150.0 million in 2025.

tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text:
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company’s effective tax rate was 25.6% compared to 23.5% in the three months ended September 30, 2025. The higher effective tax rate in the three months ended September 30, 2026 is primarily driven by increased withholding taxes associated with foreign earnings growth, including Brazil’s 10% withholding tax implemented in the fourth quarter of 2025, and increased valuation allowances associated with European restructuring costs. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company's effective tax rate was 25.0% compared to 23.9% in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The higher effective tax rate is primarily driven by increased withholding taxes associated with foreign earnings, while the nine months ended September 30, 2025 included a benefit associated with the statute of limitations expiring on a previously unrecognized tax position.

We are monitoring pending legislative developments in Luxembourg, including the Draft Budget Law currently before parliament, which would eliminate the 17-year limitation on tax loss carryforwards and reduce the corporate income tax rate. Because the legislation had not been enacted as of September 30, 2026, no impact has been reflected in our financial statements.

ocf.text: Operating Activities — Net cash provided by operating activities increased $46.2 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily driven by higher 2026 earnings coupled with lower incentive payments in 2026 associated with 2025 performance. These increases were partially offset by the 2025 impairment of SAP S/4HANA for $71.6 million, a $34.0 million insurance recovery related to our remediation of the Calvert City site in 2025 as well as higher 2026 restructuring payments.

capex.text: Investing Activities — Net cash used in investing activities during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $66.4 million and $64.2 million, respectively, which reflects the impact of capital expenditures.

Color, Additives and Inks.heading: Color, Additives and Inks
Color, Additives and Inks.text:
Sales increased $41.6 million, or 8.2%, in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the prior-year quarter, with growth across all end markets primarily driven by favorable sales mix and pricing. Our packaging and consumer end markets contributed 3.4% and 1.0%, respectively, to the segment’s sales growth, driven by demand for functional additives and color solutions used in food, beverage and personal care applications. Building & construction contributed 1.5%, driven by commercial infrastructure investment.

Sales increased $85.6 million, or 5.5%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the prior-year period. Excluding a favorable foreign currency impact of 2.3%, organic sales increased 3.2%, primarily driven by favorable sales mix and pricing actions to offset inflation. Packaging contributed 2.2% to the segment’s sales growth driven by demand for functional additives and color solutions used in food, beverage and personal care applications. Building and construction contributed 0.7% to the segment’s sales growth driven by commercial infrastructure investment.

Operating income increased $14.9 million and $29.3 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

Specialty Engineered Materials.heading: Specialty Engineered Materials
Specialty Engineered Materials.text:
Sales increased $42.9 million, or 14.4%, in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the prior-year quarter, primarily driven by increased demand for our growth vectors, favorable sales mix and pricing actions to offset inflation in input costs. Defense, the segment’s largest end market, contributed 2.5% to sales growth amid higher government defense spending. Industrial and consumer contributed 2.4% and 1.7%, respectively, reflecting new business wins and favorable pricing and mix. Telecommunications contributed 2.2% driven by high-performance computing applications. Energy and building & construction contributed 2.1% and 1.8%, respectively, driven by commercial infrastructure investment, while healthcare contributed 1.7%, driven by demand for remote monitoring and drug delivery applications.

Sales increased $68.9 million, or 7.4%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the prior-year period. Favorable foreign currency impacts contributed 1.6%, while organic sales increased 5.8%, reflecting higher demand and pricing actions to offset inflation in input costs. Growth was broad-based across nearly all end markets.

profile.name: AVIENT CORP
profile.industry: Plastic Materials, Synth Resins & Nonvulcan Elastomers

intro.text: We are an innovator of materials solutions to help our customers succeed, while enabling a sustainable world. Our products include specialty engineered materials, performance fibers, advanced composites and color and additive solutions. We are also a highly specialized developer and manufacturer of performance enhancing additives, liquid colorants and silicone colorants. When used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the terms “we,” “us,” “our," "Avient" and the “Company” mean Avient Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries. Avient was formed as PolyOne Corporation on August 31, 2000, from the consolidation of The Geon Company (Geon) and M.A. Hanna Company (Hanna). Through a series of acquisitions, divestitures, operational improvements and cultural shifts, the Company has transformed to become an innovator of materials solutions.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.
